body.statement: For every integer \(k\ge2\), every \(K\ge1\), every \(R>1\), and every \(\eta>0\), some sufficiently small \(h\in(0,R-1)\) makes the fully specified law \(P_h\), with \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independent of the Gaussian potential-outcome system and \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\), a member of \(\mathcal M_{2k,k}(1,K,1,R)\). Its arm variances and its conditional scales on every proper active subset are unequal, and \[\gamma_k(F;P_h)\le\frac{k}{1+(k-1)KR}+\eta.\] Consequently, both \(K\) and \(R\) are necessary factors, and \(1/(KR)\) is the largest lower certificate depending only on \((K,R)\) that holds uniformly over dimensions and budgets.
body.justification: The realizable unequal-scale family certifies that neither condition factor is a proof artifact and closes the dimension-free minimax comparison.
body.gap: Bian et al. construct abstract tight set functions, but do not show that such bad geometry is realizable by a legal Gaussian causal conditional-transport model.
body.consumer: Method developers learn exactly which covariance and residual margins must improve to obtain a stronger dimension-free selection guarantee.
